reader.requirement: At 85, the FD clauses that follow file-name-1 (BLOCK CONTAINS, RECORD in all three forms, LABEL RECORDS, VALUE OF, DATA RECORDS, LINAGE, CODE-SET, and the IPC module's EXTERNAL and GLOBAL) must be accepted in any order, each taking effect; order freedom does not license a repeated clause or a later edition's clause.

edition-consulted.switches: row.At(DialectLevel) picks the edition's figure; the FD row has no Earlier figure and Sequence null, so order is free at every edition
FORMAT clause introduction gate (2002); refused at 85

reader.edition-search: read the FD row of ClauseCardinalities (no Earlier) and ClauseList.At, and grepped the FD grammar (a plain '+' list, no predicate)
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for order. The clause SET differs (LABEL, VALUE OF and DATA RECORDS removed at 2002, FORMAT added at 2002), which is outside this rule
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf22_01 covers the reverse printed order for two FDs. It does not cover VALUE OF, RECORD VARYING ... DEPENDING, BLOCK ... TO ... CHARACTERS, EXTERNAL/GLOBAL interleaved, or a scrambled non-reverse order

probes.expected: two FDs with every 1985 clause scrambled (CODE-SET, LINAGE, DATA, VALUE OF, LABEL, RECORD, BLOCK; and RECORD VARYING DEPENDING ON first) accepted; the variable record written at length 7 and read back
RECORD / IS GLOBAL / LABEL / IS EXTERNAL in mixed order accepted at 85

probes.printed: COBOL0900: the FORMAT clause requires COBOL-2002 (targeting COBOL-85), plus COBOL7342 citing §2002:13.3.4.2 SR5
COBOL2423: the clause 'BLOCK CONTAINS 1 RECORDS' is written 2 times
probes.expected: any order, but each bracketed clause once

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.3.2.3 SR2  (3.2.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2

reader.notes: The grammar is an unordered '+' list, and the cardinality row's Sequence is null with no 1985 figure, so no out-of-order refusal can fire at 85. Side observation: at 85 the FORMAT refusal also emits a COBOL7342 cascade citing a 2002 rule, which is a second diagnostic for one fault.

refuter.evidence: r5j.cob (runs/r5j-001): FD F1 DATA RECORDS / CODE-SET / IS EXTERNAL / VALUE OF FILE-ID IS FID (a data-name operand) / RECORD CONTAINS 4 TO 12 CHARACTERS / LABEL RECORDS ARE OMITTED / BLOCK CONTAINS 3 RECORDS, and FD F2 LABEL RECORD STANDARD / IS GLOBAL / BLOCK 24 CHARACTERS / RECORD 6 TO 12 (CONTAINS and CHARACTERS omitted, as the 1985 format allows) / DATA RECORD R2: accepted, writes 12- and 4-character records and reads back 1:ABCDEFGHIJKL 2:WXYZ. r5a (scrambled) and r5d (the same clauses in printed order) both end with I-O status 39 on the OPEN INPUT, and r5g (r5d without LINAGE) runs, so the failure is order-independent: it is the LINAGE file read back (r5k: OPEN/WRITE/CLOSE OUTPUT of LINAGE with RECORD 4 TO 12 all 00; r5i: a fixed LINAGE file read back gives a misaligned record at 85 and 2023 alike), a print-file reread outside this rule. r5c.cob (runs/r5c-001): LABEL RECORDS written twice around RECORD refused COBOL2423. r5b.cob (runs/r5b-001): the later IS EXTERNAL AS literal phrase refused at 85 COBOL0900. cite: OK  §1985:VII.3.2.3 SR2  (3.2.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2.
